suggestions.title: "The tool: Uridine monophosphate (UMP). There's no study showing ..."

edits.before: The tool:Uridine monophosphate (UMP). The best evidence is not "UMP cures DAWS"; that study does not exist. The evidence is more basic: uridine, choline, and DHA are circulating precursors for brain phosphatide / synaptic membrane synthesis. Wurtman's group has shown that DHA + uridine + choline can increase synaptic membrane components and synaptic proteins, that DHA-induced dendritic spine formation is enhanced by UMP in animals, and that dietary UMP increased potassium-evoked dopamine release and neurite outgrowth in aged rats. So the mechanism is plausible, but the DAWS use is still a cautious human extrapolation plus anecdote.
edits.after: The tool: Uridine monophosphate (UMP). There's no study showing that "UMP cures DAWS", only more basic research on what uridine, choline, and DHA do in the brain. All three get carried in the blood to the brain, which uses them to make the fatty membranes at its synapses (circulating precursors for brain phosphatide / synaptic membrane synthesis). Wurtman's research group found that [giving the three together can increase synaptic membrane components and synaptic proteins](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4011061/), and that in animals, adding UMP to DHA made the neurons grow more new connection points ([DHA-induced dendritic spine formation](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2140951/)). And [old rats that got UMP in their food released more dopamine when their neurons were stimulated with potassium, and grew more nerve fibers](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16055952/). So it's plausible that it works on the synapses this way, but using it for DAWS in people means carefully extrapolating from those studies and from anecdotes like Scott's.

suggestions.title: "Scott's signal: Scott already had choline from eggs ..."

edits.before: Scott's signal: Scott already had choline from eggs and DHA/EPA from fish oil. After adding standard-dose UMP, he got a striking response within a day: vivid dreams returned, real childhood memories came back in dreams, psychedelic tolerance seemed to drop, and ketamine/LSD craving fell hard. That does not prove UMP rebuilt D3 receptors overnight. It does suggest that, in the right person, UMP can be a very clean signal that the synaptic-membrane / dopamine-receptor-recovery axis was starved.
edits.after: Scott added a standard dose of UMP, and within a day his ketamine/LSD cravings fell hard. He already had choline covered with eggs, and took fish oil for DHA/EPA. His psychedelic tolerance seemed to drop too. You can't tell from this whether UMP rebuilt his D3 receptors overnight. It does suggest that in the right person, UMP can show you very clearly when the brain's system for rebuilding synaptic membranes and recovering dopamine receptors has been starved of building materials. Scott was having vivid dreams again too, with real childhood memories coming back in them.

suggestions.title: "Precautions/Side Effects: Do not use concurrently with opioids and/or kratom ..."

edits.before: Precautions/Side Effects: Do not use concurrently with opioids and/or kratom (will reduce tolerance), clonidine and/or guanfacine, blood pressure lowering medications, nitrates, PDE-5 inhibitors, MAOIs, or other complex "psych" stacks without having a physician competent to consider the likelihoods of problematic interactions. Not recommended for use in pregnancy or breast-feeding. Use with extreme caution in those with bipolar disorder, prior psychotic episode, unstable panic disorder, lower end blood pressure, kidney or liver issues, or those with a currently-high likelihood of relapsing in addictions.
edits.after: Precautions/Side Effects: Do not use concurrently with opioids and/or kratom (will reduce tolerance), clonidine and/or guanfacine, blood pressure lowering medications (including nitrates and PDE-5 inhibitors), or other complex "psych" stacks without having a physician competent to consider the likelihoods of problematic interactions. Not recommended for use in pregnancy or breast-feeding. Use with extreme caution in those with a prior psychotic episode, lower end blood pressure, or kidney or liver issues.

suggestions.title: "Rule: do not take 5-HTP on the same day as psychedelics ..."

edits.before: Rule: do not take 5-HTP on the same day as psychedelics, and do not use it anywhere near ayahuasca/harmalas or iboga unless the whole medicine plan has been medically reviewed. Uridine is not serotonergic, but it may still change dream vividness, visual sensitivity, craving, and psychedelic tolerance. Do not take UMP on the same day as psychedelics; if sensitivity changes, assume your old psychedelic dose may now be too high.

suggestions.title: "Side effects / stop signs: The most common problem is the "choline headache" ..."

edits.before: Side effects / stop signs: The most common problem is the "choline headache" or spaced-out brain fog: if UMP accelerates membrane synthesis while choline availability is low, the system can feel under-supplied. Other stop signs include insomnia, jitteriness, racing thoughts, irritability, emotional flatness, nausea, stomach cramps, or loose stools. If it makes you wired, numb, or weirdly irritable, stop. Do not push through.
edits.after: Side effects / stop signs: In practice, the most common problem is the "choline headache" or spaced-out brain fog. It isn't in the studies, but the likely reason is that if UMP accelerates membrane synthesis while choline availability is low, the system can feel under-supplied. Other stop signs include insomnia, jitteriness, racing thoughts, irritability, emotional flatness, nausea, stomach cramps, or loose stools. If it makes you wired, numb, or weirdly irritable, stop. Do not push through.

suggestions.title: "Dose: 300–600 mg/day, taken earlier in the day ..."

edits.before: Dose: 300–600 mg/day, taken earlier in the day. Below ~300 mg the cortisol effect is unreliable; above ~800 mg adds nothing.
edits.after: Dose: about 400 mg/day, taken earlier in the day. In the stress studies, which used a PS complex, 400 mg blunted the cortisol response, while 200 mg did nothing and 600 or 800 mg didn't either.

edits.before: Phosphatidylserine 300–600 mg earlier in the day only if you fit the high-cortisol profile + 1 cup broccoli sprouts + Magnesium Glycinate 400 mg + NAC 1.8–2.4 g divided.
edits.after: Phosphatidylserine about 400 mg earlier in the day only if you fit the high-cortisol profile + 1 cup broccoli sprouts + Magnesium Glycinate 400 mg + NAC 1.8–2.4 g divided.

suggestions.what: The PS dose as about 400 mg, the dose that worked in the stress studies, here and in the Timeline.
suggestions.why: In [Hellhammer 2004](https://doi.org/10.1080/10253890410001728379), 400 mg of a PS complex blunted the cortisol response to stress and 600 and 800 mg didn't; in [Hellhammer 2014](https://doi.org/10.1186/1476-511X-13-121), 400 mg worked only in chronically stressed men with an over-reactive stress response, and 200 mg did nothing. Small studies. The post's "above ~800 mg adds nothing" doesn't fit them: 600 mg already didn't work.
suggestions.deciding: Whether the dose becomes about 400 mg, in both places.
suggestions.stays: Earlier in the day, and "only if you fit the high-cortisol profile".

suggestions.title: "The Mandate: You must hit 4,700 mg of Potassium daily."

edits.before: The Mandate: You must hit 4,700 mg of Potassium daily.
edits.after: The Target: Aim for 4,700 mg of Potassium daily.

suggestions.what: "must hit" as "aim for", and "The Mandate" as "The Target".
suggestions.why: 4,700 mg is a target for healthy people, and falling short of it doesn't mean you're deficient ([Kumssa 2021](https://doi.org/10.3390/nu13041369)). It's also the older US figure: since 2019 the adequate intake is 3,400 mg a day for men and 2,600 mg for women ([Tufts Health & Nutrition Letter](https://www.nutritionletter.tufts.edu/?p=2056)).
suggestions.deciding: Whether "must" becomes "aim for". The 4,700 mg stays unless you'd rather use the 2019 figures.
suggestions.stays: The number, and "The Source: Food Only."
suggestions.found_by: The warnings checks, 4 November (the bad-trips lane's agmatine check, and the rest in WARNINGS-CHECK.md)

suggestions.title: "The Source: Food Only. (Supplements are dangerous and limited to 99mg)."

edits.before: The Source: Food Only. (Supplements are dangerous and limited to 99mg).
edits.after: The Source: Food Only. (Supplements are limited to 99mg, and bigger doses need a doctor's supervision.)

suggestions.what: "dangerous" said as what the evidence shows: bigger doses need supervision.
suggestions.why: In a trial of 1,200 people with implanted defibrillators, supervised potassium supplements held their potassium high-normal and cut the main risk outcome, about 23% against 29% ([Danielsen 2026](https://doi.org/10.1093/europace/euag272)). So supplements aren't dangerous as such; that trial's were supervised.

suggestions.title: "Warning: Direct D-Serine carries a higher renal (kidney) load than L-Serine ..."

edits.before: Warning: Direct D-Serine carries a higher renal (kidney) load than L-Serine. Do not exceed 30mg/kg and ensure high water intake. This risk is compounded by the higher renal load caused by a keto diet or high protein intake.
edits.after: Warning: High doses of D-Serine damaged the kidneys in rat studies, so it carries a kidney caution, though kidney problems have been rare in human studies. Do not exceed 30mg/kg and ensure high water intake.

suggestions.what: The kidney warning said as what the studies found, and the keto and high-protein sentence cut.
suggestions.why: In rats, D-serine damages the kidneys at high doses; across the human studies one person had abnormal kidney values, which cleared in days, and nobody has compared it with L-serine in people ([Meftah 2021](https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyt.2021.726365)). Nothing supports keto or protein adding to it ([the warnings check](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/claude/community-joel-1018/articles/neuro-de-armoring/humanize/fix-20261104/warnings/WARNINGS-CHECK.md), item 24).
suggestions.deciding: Whether the warning reads this way and the keto sentence goes. The 30 mg/kg stays (the highest dose tested in people was 120 mg/kg, so it's a cautious choice), and so does the water; both are your call.
